RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 50

An all-male panel alongside selecting a less-experienced male candidate can suggest affinity bias or an "old boys' club" culture. However, head-of-group positions heavily prioritize commercial acumen and client relationships over technical tenure, which may explain the decision.

Do not raise the panel’s gender directly if your goal is receiving constructive feedback or protecting professional relationships; doing so will likely trigger defensive silence or legal caution from HR. Instead, send a polite, neutral follow-up requesting standard feedback. 

If you suspect unlawful sex discrimination and intend to pursue a formal grievance or legal claim, consult an employment lawyer first. In that context, the panel's composition and the experience disparity serve as relevant circumstantial evidence.
